subject: Suggestions (beta) — Support FAQ wording + escalation path (review)
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 4:12 PM
Subject: Suggestions (beta) — Support FAQ wording + escalation path (review)
Attachments: Suggestions_Beta_Support_FAQ_v0.3.docx

Hey all — attaching a draft Support FAQ for the Console > Optimize > Suggestions (beta).

Asks:
1) Please sanity check wording around “estimated savings” and “risk” so we don’t overpromise.
2) Confirm the escalation path + internal owners for common issues (insufficient telemetry, savings changed week-to-week, “High risk” complaints).
3) Anything missing for Support readiness before we enable the first cohort.

I pulled in some language from the current docs draft, but this FAQ is the thing Support will paste into tickets, so it needs to be crisp.

Target: comments back EOD Monday so we can publish to the Support KB before the cohort enablement.

Thanks,
Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product — Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference



From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 5:01 PM
Subject: Re: Suggestions (beta) — Support FAQ wording + escalation path (review)

Reviewed quickly. Overall solid. A few edits I’d strongly recommend (Support copy tone + avoid guarantees):

- Anywhere we say “will reduce cost” → “can reduce cost” / “is expected to reduce cost”.
- Add a one-liner definition of “estimate” = based on last N days of observed traffic + current pricing + modeled effect of caching/batching.
- Explicitly call out: estimated savings may change as traffic mix, sequence lengths, or cache hit rate changes (this is driving SUP-19344).

Escalation proposal (for the FAQ + internal runbook):
1) Support triage: confirm tenant/workspace, route/model, and screenshot of the suggestion drawer (esp. “Basis of estimate”).
2) If “insufficient telemetry”: check whether tenant has met baseline thresholds (traffic volume + freshness). If unclear, escalate to Telemetry (Logan) with tenant + time window.
3) If “High risk is vague” or customer wants reasons: point to rationale bullets; if still unhappy, loop in CS owner + file note for Product.
4) If any signs of cross-tenant data exposure (even suspected): STOP and escalate to Security + on-call immediately.

Happy to help tighten the canned responses once we agree on the official path.

-Dev

Dev Patel
Support Readiness Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 5:34 PM
Subject: Re: Suggestions (beta) — Support FAQ wording + escalation path (review)

+1 to Dev’s edits.

From the Enterprise CS angle: we should add a specific note in the FAQ for “Read-only beta” since customers keep asking for one-click apply.

Suggested FAQ Q/A to add:

Q: Can Redwood apply this suggestion for me?
A: Not in the beta. Suggestions are read-only today. Your team can implement the change in your Redwood config (or we can walk you through it). We’re working on an “apply with guardrails” flow in a later phase.

Also, for escalations: for beta cohort accounts, I’d like Support to loop the assigned CSM/TAM before we tell the customer “engineering is investigating.” Keeps messaging consistent.

Miguel — can you confirm the cohort accounts you’re owning so we can list who gets looped for what?

Rachel

Rachel Kim
Enterprise CS Rollout Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Nair <asha.nair@brightflag.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 6:22 PM
Subject: Suggestions (beta) — quick check on FAQ wording for “estimated savings”
Attachments: Suggestions_Beta_Support_FAQ_v0.3.docx

Hi Asha —

Looping you in briefly since BrightFlag is in our initial Suggestions beta cohort.

We’re finalizing a short Support FAQ that our team uses when you open tickets during the beta (e.g., “why did the savings change?” / “what does high risk mean?”). If you have 10 minutes, could you skim the attached and tell me if any phrasing feels unclear or overconfident?

Two specific spots we’re debating:
- “Estimated savings” language (we want it to be actionable but not a promise)
- Risk definitions (low/medium/high) and whether the reasons are concrete enough

No need for line edits unless you want to — even “this feels vague” is helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa



From: Asha Nair <asha.nair@brightflag.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 8:11 AM
Subject: Re: Suggestions (beta) — quick check on FAQ wording for “estimated savings”

Hi Marissa,

Skimmed — overall good.

Two reactions from our side (platform team):

1) The word “confidence” shows up once but isn’t defined. We’d like either a definition or to avoid the term entirely (it reads like a statistical guarantee).

2) The “High risk” section is better with the bullets, but I’d suggest explicitly stating what kind of risk it is (latency vs quality vs cost variance). Even if it’s just: “High risk often means higher chance of impacting p95 latency or quality for your specific traffic mix; see rationale bullets.”

Otherwise, the “savings may change week-to-week” explanation is exactly what we needed.

Thanks,
Asha

Asha Nair
Staff Platform Engineer
BrightFlag AI



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 9:31 AM
Subject: Re: Suggestions (beta) — Support FAQ wording + escalation path (review)
Attachments: Suggestions_Beta_Support_FAQ_v0.4.docx

Thanks all — incorporated edits + Asha’s feedback into v0.4 (attached).

Changes made:
- Swapped “will reduce” → “can / expected to reduce” throughout.
- Added a tighter definition of estimate inputs (observed traffic window + modeled effect; may change with traffic mix/freshness).
- Removed the stray “confidence” mention (wasn’t defined).
- Updated High risk FAQ to explicitly name risk categories (latency / quality / variance) and point Support to the rationale bullets in the drawer (aligns with SUP-19402 theme).
- Added the “read-only beta / no one-click apply yet” answer (good call Rachel).

Escalation path section in the FAQ now:
- Standard Support triage checklist
- Loop CSM/TAM for beta cohort accounts before customer-facing “eng investigating”
- Telemetry escalation guidance for “insufficient telemetry” (SUP-19361)
- Security stop-the-line note for any tenant scoping concerns

Naomi — can you do a quick pass on the “usage/cost exposure” paragraph to ensure we’re consistent with the security review guidance? If yes, we’ll post this to the Support KB Monday.

Marissa

(Refs for context: SUP-19344, SUP-19361, SUP-19402, INT-884)
